title: cost-optimization: autotune batching/caching defaults + quant profiles + uecon tooling
author: Ava Martinez
description: Context: This PR implements an end-to-end cost optimization automation iteration: improved default batching and KV-caching heuristics, new quantization profile plumbing and defaults, and a first-pass unit-economics (uecon) tooling integration to surface per-token cost estimates. Motivation: production workloads show excessive small-batch requests and suboptimal quant profile selection leading to 12-18% higher token cost on average. The goal is to provide safer defaults and observability so teams get immediate cost wins without manual tuning. Changes: 1) Runtime: autotune module now computes per-route default batch_size and cache_prefix_threshold based on recent latency and sequence-length histograms; adds a low-risk fallback policy to avoid regressions. 2) Caching: improved KV cache eviction policy and prefix fingerprinting to increase cache hits for conversational workloads. 3) Quantization: introduce quant profile metadata, new CLI to generate recommended profiles (fast/compatible/aggressive), and runtime selection heuristics. 4) Uecon tooling: add a microservice that consumes request traces and produces per-route unit cost estimates, surfaced in the console and exposed via a simple API for automation. 5) Docs + tests: operator docs for new settings, dashboard screenshots, and expanded perf/regression tests. Rollout plan: staged canary on Dedicated, gradual rollout to Hosted with metrics-based automatic rollback. Related: ENG-8421, ENG-8475, SUP-1210. Checklist: - [x] Runtime heuristics implemented - [x] Quant profile generation + selection - [x] Uecon estimator service + API - [x] Integration tests and perf baselines - [x] Docs and console wiring - [x] Canaries configured and playbook updated

Ava Martinez (2026-02-03): Added route-level opt-out and explicit SLA pin to skip autotune/quant selection; updated console UI to surface the pin.
Liam O'Connor (2026-02-10): CI perf job showed a small regression for short-context chat tests; is that expected?
Ava Martinez (2026-02-11): Investigated: regression due to cache eviction threshold; tuned parameters and added regression test; perf now back to baseline.
